name: WORKDAY.INTL
description: WORKDAY.INTL returns the date that is a given number of working days before or after a start date, with a customizable weekend (a weekend code or a 7-character string) and optional holidays.
tldr: Returns a date n workdays away with a custom weekend.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: The number of workdays to move. Positive moves forward, negative moves backward. The start date itself is not counted.

parameters.name: weekend
parameters.description: Optional. A number 1-7 or 11-17 selecting weekend days (1 = Sat+Sun default, 2 = Sun only, 3 = Mon only, ... 7 = Fri only, 11 = Sun+Mon, ... 17 = Sat+Sun), or a 7-character string of 0/1 for Mon-Sun where 1 means weekend.

parameters.name: holidays
parameters.description: Optional range or array of dates to exclude as non-working days.

basicExample.description: Five workdays after Jan 1, 2024 (default Sat/Sun weekend)
basicExample.explanation: With the default weekend (code 1, Sat+Sun), five workdays from Monday Jan 1 land on Monday Jan 8 2024 (serial 45298).

advancedExamples.title: Custom weekend via string (Mon and Sun off)
advancedExamples.scenario: A schedule where Monday and Sunday are non-working
advancedExamples.description: A 7-character string sets the weekend pattern
advancedExamples.explanation: The string "1000001" marks Monday and Sunday as weekends (Mon-Sun order). Five workdays from Jan 1 land on Saturday Jan 6 (serial 45296), since Mon and Sun are skipped.

advancedExamples.title: Sunday-only weekend via code
advancedExamples.description: Weekend code 2 treats only Sunday as non-working
advancedExamples.explanation: With only Sunday off, five consecutive workdays (Jan 1-5, none of which is Sunday) land on Friday Jan 5 2024 (serial 45295).

howItWorks: WORKDAY.INTL walks from start_date counting only days that are not designated weekends by the weekend argument, also skipping listed holidays, until it reaches the requested number of workdays. The weekend can be a preset code or a 7-character 0/1 string in Monday-to-Sunday order.

howToSteps.name: Enter the start date
howToSteps.text: Provide a date serial or DATE(...) expression.

howToSteps.name: Enter the number of workdays
howToSteps.text: Use a positive or negative integer.

howToSteps.name: Set the weekend
howToSteps.text: Use a code (1-7/11-17) or a 7-char 0/1 string (Mon-Sun).

howToSteps.name: Optionally list holidays
howToSteps.text: Pass a range or array of holiday dates.

limitations: Available only in Excel 2010 and later.
The weekend string must be exactly seven characters in Monday-to-Sunday order.
The start date itself is not counted toward the days total.

commonErrors.cause: The weekend string is not exactly seven 0/1 characters.
commonErrors.fix: Use a valid 7-character string such as "0000011".

commonErrors.cause: An invalid weekend code (not 1-7 or 11-17) was supplied.
commonErrors.fix: Use a supported weekend code or a valid string.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: WORKDAY.INTL is available in Google Sheets with identical syntax, codes, and the 7-character weekend string.

faq.question: What does the weekend string mean?
faq.answer: It is seven characters for Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun, where 1 marks a weekend day, e.g. "0000011" = Sat+Sun off.

faq.question: Which code is the default?
faq.answer: Code 1, meaning Saturday and Sunday are weekends.
